title: View transition disambiguation
blurb: Runs document.startViewTransition() across three named cards (including escaped \31 st-pick), collects ::view-transition-group() CSSPseudoElement objects, and compares type, selectorText, and KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement.
question: Can selectorText disambiguate multiple ::view-transition-group() objects—including identifiers that require CSS escaping—and drive per-group animations where KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement fails?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless across three shuffles: all three group objects report the same .type ('::view-transition-group'), and KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement returns unescaped '::view-transition-group(1st-pick)' which html.pseudo() rejects as null. Spotlight animation runs in labelled fallback mode in Chrome 153 until selectorText ships in Chrome 160+.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (live startViewTransition); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement reports view-transition names unescaped, breaking round-tripping for identifiers starting with a digit
friction.repro: Set view-transition-name: \31 st-pick on an element, start a view transition, read effect.pseudoElement ('::view-transition-group(1st-pick)'), and pass it to document.documentElement.pseudo(); it returns null because 1st-pick is not a valid unescaped CSS identifier.
friction.workaround: Use CSSPseudoElement.selectorText (which escapes via SerializeIdentifier as '::view-transition-group(\31 st-pick)') or escape known names with CSS.escape().
